evidence.description: The workflow aggregates each module's repeated daily logs before any inferential procedure: collapse_to_modules reduces the six rows per planter to one record containing a screened mean, an open mean, and their contrast, yielding exactly one analysed row per independent unit (module_id).
evidence.observed_value: 14 module-level records built from per-module fmean of screened days and open days

source_refs.quoted_text:
def collapse_to_modules(logs):
    """Reduce each module's repeated logging days to one analysed row."""
    records = []
    for unit in sorted({unit for unit, _state in logs}):
        screened_days = logs[(unit, SCREENED)]
        open_days = logs[(unit, OPEN_TOP)]
        screened_mean = fmean(screened_days)
        open_mean = fmean(open_days)

evidence.description: The paired t-test is run on the module-level aggregates, not on the raw session rows: the lists passed to scipy.stats.ttest_rel are built from `records` (one element per module), so the row-independent procedure receives 14 paired values, one per independent unit.
evidence.observed_value: stats.ttest_rel applied to 14 per-module screened means vs 14 per-module open means

source_refs.quoted_text:
The 84 session rows are repeated measurements rather than 84 independent
observations: six of them belong to each planter. Every module's three
screened days and three open days were therefore averaged first, and the
module-level contrast (screened mean minus open mean) was what entered the
test. That leaves exactly one analysed row per planter module, so the units
in the reported comparison are the 14 modules, not the 84 daily logs.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by tracing every path from the 84 raw session rows to the inferential procedure. The only call to a statistical test is stats.ttest_rel(screened, open_top) in build_report, and both arguments are list comprehensions over `records`, the output of collapse_to_modules, which contains exactly one element per distinct module_id (14 elements). The raw per-day lists from read_sessions are consumed only by fmean within collapse_to_modules and by the n_sessions row count; no test statistic touches them directly. I also checked the reported output for signatures of pseudoreplication: degrees of freedom are 13 (consistent with n = 14 modules, not 83 for 84 rows), and recomputing t from the 14 tabled contrasts (mean -0.350, SD 0.210) yields about -6.24, matching the reported -6.22, whereas a test on 84 rows would produce a different df and a substantially different statistic. I further spot-verified the module-level means in the report table against the raw CSV (P01 and others) and confirmed the aggregation is faithful. The attempt to falsify the 'no issue' conclusion failed on every check.
